logline: In a 2071 South Korea reduced to wasteland by a comet's aftermath, elite delivery drivers called Black Knights are the last lifeline of a suffocating population - and one legendary courier may be the only person capable of dismantling the corporate empire profiting from humanity's desperation.

renewal.note: Six-episode limited series completed on Netflix in May 2023. No renewal announced; created as a self-contained story based on the webtoon by Lee Yun-kyun.

bollymeter.basis: A 69% Tomatometer from 16 critics reflects a show that delivers efficient dystopian action with Kim Woo-bin commanding the screen, while critics noted the world-building outpaces the character depth.

pull_quotes.text: As dystopian escapism goes, the series delivers thrill, spills and chills with dead-eyed efficiency.
Imagine that your Ocado driver is Tom Hardy in Mad Max: Fury Road, and you won't be far off.

seasons.review_body: Black Knight arrived on Netflix in May 2023 adapting Lee Yun-kyun's webtoon into a six-episode dystopian sprint. The premise is audacious: set forty years after a comet has rendered most of South Korea uninhabitable, survivors depend on oxygen delivered by armoured couriers called Black Knights. Kim Woo-bin commands the action as the near-mythical 5-8, and the stunt choreography drew consistent admiration. Critics at 69% Tomatometer on 16 reviews found the show accomplished in its genre pleasures while thin on emotional depth - the Guardian compared it to Tom Hardy in Mad Max, and the Daily Telegraph praised its efficient thrills. The IMDb audience score of 6.4 and RT audience score of 76% suggest viewers found more to enjoy than critics did, particularly those who came for the action spectacle and class-allegory overtones. At six tight episodes it never overstays its welcome.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces the oxygen-scarcity dystopia with confident world-building: the visual design is striking, the class stratification between citizens and refugees is immediate, and Kim Woo-bin's 5-8 establishes himself as an action archetype worth following across six tight episodes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: 5-8's first delivery run through the wasteland - the show announces its action grammar and its bleak beauty in a single sequence.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 6
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale consolidates the dystopian allegory with a showdown between 5-8 and the corporate villains controlling the oxygen supply. The action delivers; the resolution leans on spectacle over emotional weight, which mirrors the season's strengths and limitations in miniature.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The climactic confrontation that frames delivery drivers as the last line of resistance against a privatised survival economy.
